function.description: Executes a call to a specified Web API endpoint with given parameters and returns the response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

endpoint.description: The URL of the Web API endpoint to be called.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the API call.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested or submitted.

params.description: Query parameters to be appended to the endpoint URL.

query.description: The search term for the query.

body.description: The JSON payload to be sent with POST, PUT, or PATCH requests.

data.description: The actual data to be sent in the request body.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for a server response before timing out. This is a float type value.

Sure thing! Finding a three‑bedroom flat in Zürich can feel overwhelming because the city’s housing market moves fast—especially when you’re looking at larger units. Below I’ve broken down everything from what you’ll likely pay in each district to where to look online, plus a quick “cheat sheet” so you know exactly what to do next. --- ## 1️⃣ Quick Snapshot – What You Can Expect | District / Area | Typical Monthly Rent* | Notes | |-----------------|-----------------------|-------| | **Zürich City Centre** (e.g., Kreis 1–7) | CHF 2 200 – 3 500+ | Premium locations, close to transit & services. | | **Oerlikon / Zollikon** | CHF 1 800 – 2 700 | Good mix of modern apartments, slightly cheaper than centre. | | **Wollishofen / Hirslanden** | CHF 1 600 – 2 400 | Family-friendly, quieter suburbs. | | **Langstrasse / Seebach** | CHF 1 300 – 2 000 | Trendy, nightlife, more affordable. | | **Uetliberg / Adliswil** | CHF 1 100 – 1 900 | Suburban vibe, great views, still within commute time. | \*Rents vary widely depending on exact size, floor level, furnishings, year built, and whether utilities are included. For a *three‑bedroom* unit, expect roughly 20% higher rents compared to two‑bedrooms in the same area. > ⚠️ **Tip:** In Zürich it’s common for landlords to charge a separate “service fee” (often ~CHF 50–70/month). Make sure this is factored into your total cost estimate. --- ## 2️⃣ Where to Search Online | Platform | Why It Works | How To Filter | |----------|--------------|---------------| | **Homegate.ch** | Largest Swiss portal, extensive filter options including “number of rooms”, “floor plan”, “pet friendly”. | Set `Rooms ≥ 3`, choose your preferred district(s), add “Pet Friendly” if applicable. | | **ImmoScout24.ch** | Strong mobile app + email alerts. Offers “price drop” notifications. | Same filtering logic; enable push/email alerts for instant updates. | | **Newhome.ch** | Focuses on rentals, often lists newer developments first. | Look under “Apartment Rentals > 3 Rooms.” | | **Comparis.ch** | Aggregates listings across multiple sites → one-stop shop. | Use “Search all” and apply room/price filters. | | **Immobilien.com** | Great for international buyers; offers translation support. | Similar filters; useful if you speak English only. | | **Facebook Groups** (`Wohnungen Zürich`) | Many private owners post here without agency fees. | Join, read group rules, keep an eye on daily posts. | | **Local Newspapers** (`Neue Zürcher Zeitung` classifieds) | Still active for high-end properties. | Check weekly print or digital editions. | ### 📱 Mobile Apps Worth Installing - **Homegate App** – Push notifications for newly listed 3-bed flats. - **ImmoScout24 App** – Real-time price-drop alerts. - **WhatsApp Group** – Some agencies run dedicated WhatsApp chats for urgent vacancies. --- ## 3️⃣ Practical Steps to Secure Your Apartment | Step | Action | Key Points | |------|--------|------------| | **A. Define Budget & Must-Haves** | Write down max monthly rent, required square footage (~90–120 m² typical), essential features (balcony, parking, elevator). | Include utilities & service fees in overall budget. | | **B. Create Alerts Early** | On each platform, save searches with “new listings” and “price drops.” | Turn on email/SMS alerts; many apps let you receive push notifications instantly. | | **C. Prepare Documents Quickly** | Landlords usually require:
- Proof of income (last 3 payslips)
- Employment letter
- Credit report (Schufa equivalent)
- ID copy | Have PDFs ready; upload them once you get a viewing invitation. | | **D. Schedule Viewings Strategically** | Aim for weekday mornings (8–10 AM); most landlords open their doors early.
Book back-to-back viewings to maximize efficiency. | Bring a notebook or phone camera to compare key metrics quickly. | | **E. Negotiate Smartly** | Ask about potential discounts for longer leases (>12 months).
Inquire if utilities can be bundled or excluded. | Mention willingness to sign immediately if conditions meet expectations. | | **F. Review Contract Thoroughly** | Verify
• Rental amount & payment schedule
• Security deposit (usually 3× gross monthly rent)
• Maintenance responsibilities
• Pet clauses | Consider having a bilingual lawyer review if you’re unfamiliar with German-language contracts. | | **G. Finalize Move-In Logistics** | Arrange moving company, register address (“Einwohnermeldeamt”) within 14 days, transfer utilities. | Keep receipts for tax deductions (if applicable). | --- ## 4️⃣ Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Warning Sign | Prevention Tip | |-------|-------------|----------------| | **Hidden Fees** | Unexpected “maintenance” charges after signing. | Confirm all recurring costs up front; ask landlord to itemise. | | **Overpriced Listings** | Price far above comparable units in same building/district. | Compare recent sales/rentals via Comparis or local forums. | | **Fake Ads** | Contact attempts outside official platforms, too good to be true prices. | Never wire money before seeing the place; verify through official website links. | | **Lease Terms Too Tight** | Short-term lease (<6 months) with steep penalties. | Prefer standard 12-month lease unless you truly need flexibility. | | **Utilities Excluded** | Utilities billed separately later. | Request clear breakdown of which utilities are included. | --- ## 5️⃣ Sample Script for Automated Monitoring (Optional) If you’d like to automate monitoring of new listings, here's a simple Python snippet that pulls fresh results from Homegate's RSS feed (replace `` with your custom query): ```python import feedparser from datetime import datetime, timedelta FEED_URL = f"https://www.homegate.ch/rss/search?q=&sort=latest" def fetch_new_listings(): feed = feedparser.parse(FEED_URL) now = datetime.utcnow() threshold = now - timedelta(hours=6) # last 6 hours for entry in feed.entries: published = datetime(*entry.published_parsed[:6]) if published >= threshold: title = entry.title link = entry.link summary = entry.summary print(f"[{published}] {title}\nLink: {link}\n") fetch_new_listings() ``` Run this hourly via cron or Task Scheduler, and you'll automatically see brand-new 3‑bedroom listings appear in your terminal or log file. --- ## 🚀 Next Moves 1. **Pick Two Platforms** (say Homegate + ImmoScout24) and create identical filtered searches. 2. **Set Up Email Alerts** right away. 3. **Gather All Required Docs** today—you won’t waste time waiting for paperwork during a tight window. 4. **Schedule First Viewing** tomorrow afternoon (most landlords accept walk-ins around lunch). Feel free to share your budget, preferred districts, or any other constraints, and I can tailor the list further—or even draft a short email template you can send to prospective landlords. Happy hunting!
